Minimum vertex cover = 24 − 8 = 16. The approach uses the fact that a minimum vertex cover is the complement of a maximum independent set, so with 24 vertices the answer is 24 minus the largest independent-set size.

**Lower bound on the independent set: one of size 8 exists.**
Take S = {X005, X006, X007, X010, X014, X019, X021, X022}. Checking each member's neighbours shows no edge joins two members of S:
- X005: 3, 4, 8, 9, 13, 16, 17, 18, 23
- X006: 3, 4, 8, 11, 15, 20, 23
- X007: 0, 3, 20
- X010: 0, 9, 12, 16
- X014: 1, 3, 4, 8, 11, 15, 20
- X019: 1, 8, 9, 11, 13
- X021: 0, 1, 15, 16, 18
- X022: 2, 3, 8, 9, 16, 17

So the maximum independent set has at least 8 vertices.

**Upper bound: no independent set of size 9.**
The 24 vertices split into 9 cliques:
- C1 {4, 6, 23}, C2 {8, 11, 19}, C3 {5, 13, 17}
- C4 {2, 3, 22}, C5 {0, 7}, C6 {10, 12, 16}
- C7 {1, 14, 20}, C8 {15, 21}, C9 {9, 18}

An independent set can use at most one vertex per clique. A set of size 9 would therefore need exactly one vertex from every clique. Branch on C8:

- **Choose X021.** This excludes 0, 1, 15, 16 and 18.
  - C5 is forced to X007 and C9 is forced to X009.
  - X009 excludes 10 and 12, so C6 has no available vertex. Contradiction.
- **Choose X015.** This excludes 6, 14 and 21.
  - If C9 is X018, it excludes 1, 23 and 5. Then C7 is forced to X020 and C1 to X004. But X004 and X020 are adjacent. Contradiction.
  - If C9 is X009, it excludes 10, 12, 18 and 22. Then C6 is forced to X016, which excludes X000.
  - So C5 is forced to X007, which excludes X003.
  - Now C4 = {2, 3, 22} is empty, because X016 excludes 2 and 22. Contradiction.

Every branch fails, so the maximum independent set has exactly 8 vertices.

The minimum vertex cover has **20** vertices. In any graph, a minimum vertex cover is the complement of a maximum independent set. So the work is to show the largest independent set here has 12 vertices; then the answer is 32 − 12 = 20.

**Step 1 – An independent set of size 12 exists.**
Take {X004, X005, X006, X007, X010, X011, X012, X015, X017, X023, X027, X030}. Checking each vertex's neighbour list confirms that no two of these are joined by an edge. So the maximum independent set has at least 12 vertices.

**Step 2 – No independent set has more than 12 vertices.**
- X005's only neighbours, X003 and X008, are adjacent to each other. So some maximum independent set contains X005, and we can delete X003 and X008. This leaves 29 vertices, and we must show at most 11 more can be chosen from them.
- **Case A: X002 is chosen.**
  - Choosing X002 removes X006, X009, X016, X018, X019, X020, X023 and X027.
  - The remaining 20 vertices can be covered by 9 cliques: {X007, X028, X031}, {X015, X024, X029}, {X012, X013}, {X000, X011, X026}, {X001, X017, X022}, {X010, X014, X025}, {X004}, {X021}, {X030}.
  - An independent set takes at most one vertex per clique, so at most 9 more can be chosen. That gives at most 1 + 9 = 10.
- **Case B: X002 is not chosen.**
  - X023 now has only one neighbour (X013), and X027 has only one (X021). So we may take X023 and X027 and delete X013 and X021.
  - The remaining 24 vertices can be covered by 10 cliques: {X004, X009, X016, X020}, {X007, X028, X031}, {X015, X024, X029}, {X000, X011, X026}, {X001, X017, X022}, {X012, X018}, {X014, X019, X025}, {X006}, {X010}, {X030}.
  - Reaching 10 would require one vertex from every clique, including X006, X010 and X030. But those three are neighbours of every vertex of {X014, X019, X025}, so that clique cannot be used. Hence at most 9 can be chosen, giving at most 2 + 9 = 11.
- Both cases allow at most 11 vertices besides X005, so any independent set has at most 12 vertices.

**Conclusion.** The maximum independent set has exactly 12 vertices, so the minimum vertex cover has 32 − 12 = 20.

The minimum vertex cover has **21** vertices. I found it as 32 minus the size of a maximum independent set, because the complement of a minimum vertex cover is a maximum independent set.

**Lower bound on the independent set (11 is achievable).** These 11 vertices are pairwise non-adjacent:
{X001, X006, X008, X011, X014, X015, X021, X025, X026, X027, X031}.

I checked each vertex's neighbour list, and none of these vertices is adjacent to another in the set. Its complement is therefore a vertex cover of 32 − 11 = 21 vertices.

**Upper bound on the independent set (11 is the most possible).** The 32 vertices split into 11 disjoint cliques, using only edges from the list:

| 1 | {X001, X005, X009, X029} |

These contain 4 + 8×3 + 2×2 = 32 vertices, so every vertex is covered exactly once. An independent set can include at most one vertex from each clique, so it has at most 11 vertices.

**Conclusion.** The maximum independent set has exactly 11 vertices. The minimum vertex cover therefore has 32 − 11 = 21 vertices.
